title: Volume of 3D Shapes
preview: Volume of pyramids, cones, and spheres, surface area of spheres, and working backwards from a known volume to find a missing dimension.
description: Students find the volume of pyramids, cones, and spheres and the surface area of spheres, connect each solid to a related prism or cylinder, and work backwards from a known volume to solve for a missing radius or height (Indiana 8.GM.2).

sections.label: Volume of Pyramids (Supplement)
sections.description: V = (1/3)(base area)(height); a pyramid is one-third of the prism with the same base and height.

sections.label: 9-2 Volume of Cones
sections.description: V = (1/3)πr²h; a cone is one-third of the cylinder with the same base and height.

sections.label: 9-3 Volume of Spheres
sections.description: V = (4/3)πr³; doubling the radius multiplies the volume by eight.

sections.label: Surface Area of Spheres (Supplement)
sections.description: SA = 4πr²; contrast r² surface-area growth with r³ volume growth.

sections.label: 9-4 Find Missing Dimensions
sections.description: Work backwards from a known volume to find a missing radius or height (square and cube roots).

source.name: Plug N Play
